## The chain


Dark blue runs on the cluster; purple runs anywhere, including CI; brown is
reference data extracted from PRISME.

## Two edges that carry the whole result

Both are silent failure modes — they produce complete, plausible numbers rather
than errors — so the diagram is drawn to make them visible.

::: {.callout-important}
## `track_extents` is fed from the assignment table, not from `overlap_join`

`overlap_join` clips every sample to `[t_off, t_land]`. Extents taken after it
could only ever land *inside* the interval, so boundary error would be
one-sided: a track starting before take-off or ending after landing would be
invisible, what the number measured would be sampling cadence rather than
boundary accuracy, and a track merging two flights — the failure this study
most needs to see — would score near-zero error for the merge.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Detection needs ground truth as well as `matched`

`overlap_join` is an inner join. A flight OpenSky never saw produces no rows at
all, so it is invisible to every metric computed from `matched` — including
every metric the V1 track study reported. Recovering it needs a left join from
the full ground-truth table, and it is the strongest coverage signal on this
site.
:::

## Stages

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd

man = _data.manifest()
avail = _data.periods_available()

rows = []
for period in avail:
    key = f"flight_offsets_{period}.parquet"
    e = man.get(key)
    if e is None:
        rows.append({"period": period, "state vectors": "unverified",
                     "ground-truth flights": "unverified", "arm": "unverified",
                     "produced (UTC)": "unverified", "git": "unverified"})
        continue
    inp = e.get("inputs", {})
    rows.append({
        "period": period,
        "state vectors": f"{inp.get('state_vectors', 0):,}",
        "ground-truth flights": f"{inp.get('ground_truth_flights', 0):,}",
        "arm": "recommended (A8)",
        "produced (UTC)": e.get("produced_utc", "")[:16].replace("T", " "),
        "git": e.get("git_sha", "") + ("-dirty" if e.get("git_dirty") else ""),
    })

if rows:
    display(pd.DataFrame(rows))
else:
    display(Markdown("*No committed extract yet — run `scripts/run_offsets.py`.*"))
```

Row counts come from `data/_manifest.json`, written by the job that produced
each file. They are not typed into this page, so it cannot claim a count the
run did not produce. A stage with no manifest entry renders as **unverified**.

## What runs where

| Stage | Module | Runs on | Needs credentials |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ground-truth extract | `scripts/fetch_reference.R` | work laptop | PRISME / ROracle |
| Mirror reference to S3 | `opdi/benchmarks/mirror_reference.py` | cluster | S3 |
| Segmentation + offsets | `scripts/run_offsets.py` | OSN Kubernetes | S3 |
| Aggregation | `scripts/aggregate.py` | anywhere | no |
| Page generation | `scripts/gen_pages.py` | anywhere | no |
| Render | `quarto render site` | anywhere, incl. GitHub Actions | no |

The split is the point. Only the first three need access to anything; from the
per-flight table onward the site rebuilds from committed data alone, which is
what lets CI republish it on every push.
